I started Fallout 4 expecting a smooth experience, especially since my PC is more than capable of running a game from 2015. Unfortunately, the game has been a technical mess from the start.

Pros:

1. When the game actually works, I can run it at maximum settings with excellent performance and high FPS.

Cons:

1. Frequent crashes to desktop.
2. Severe audio synchronization issues that make conversations and gameplay feel broken.
3. Audio randomly cuts out completely, requiring a full system reboot to restore sound.
4. Spent more time troubleshooting than actually playing.

It's frustrating that a game this old still suffers from such major technical problems. The few moments where everything works show the potential of the game, but constant crashes and audio issues make it difficult to recommend. A game shouldn't require this much effort just to function properly.

citations.review_text:
This game is already more than 10 years old. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I feel old!

Fallout 4! One of my most anticipated games back in 2015. I had only just gotten into this amazing franchise a few years prior thanks to New Vegas and 3 so of course I was going to be hyped as hell for this game and originally got it day one back when it came out for my Xbox One. I mean I still remember that original reveal trailer like it’s still only a few years old. And did that hype pay of? Well, in a lot of ways yes but also no in a lot of others.

Let’s just get the obvious out of the way, the severally toned down RPG elements. And I’m not just talking about the worser dialogue options you have this time around only having four to pick from using a clearly Mass Effect inspired wheel but also the karma system from 3 and New Vegas where you would gain or lose karma depending on your actions in game is gone, traits are gone, you only have perks this time for building your character, basically a lot of what drew me and a bunch of other people into Fallout originally, it’s heavy emphasis on the role playing aspects, are all but removed or over simplified. Yes, you can still choice from four different factions when doing the main story including the villains The Institute but dam do they suck as a villain. Less because of the premise behind them because I actually like the almost They Live inspired idea of having synth’s kidnap people and replace them but even if you do side with The Institute and try to ask them why they are doing it they won’t give you an actual answer and just tell you “You wouldn’t understand.” Yeah, no ♥♥♥♥ I don’t understand! I won’t tell me! So yeah, the story also isn’t the best either. And yeah, there’s also the usual Bethesda jank that’s still here even now because Bethesda refuses to move on from the engine they have been using since Morrowind that’s only being held together by duct tape!

Thing is, literally everything else about this game is fantastic! The combat is way…
Janky and buggy as hell but it just scratches an itch that other games can't. Story is ass though.
As much as I lament the degradation in writing quality and number of unique quests you can't deny FO4 is a good time

great game but the HD texture pack sucks just run it native and get visual mods from nexus for it if you wanna up the games graphics with good preformance. the story is not the greatest especially compared to Fallout 3 and New Vegas but certainly an adventure i think you can get lost in and character dialouge is pretty solid as well. i give it a 8/10 in terms of fun.

The Fallout franchise by Bethesda ain't known for their story as it's kinda boring so don't expect to be thrilled with the main quest here, the player's decisions in game feels ultimately irrelevant in the end and the characters are so lame that it's clear not much thought were given to their backstories (I'm looking at you main antagonist). The presentation of the in universe lore is inconsistent at best, the factions felt underwhelming and the overall game screams wasted potential. If you want to play an RPG with an actual story and the inclusion of player choices that matters? Play Baldurs Gate or Mass Effect instead.

So despite it's dogwater story among many of it's flaws, why is Fallout 4 one of my favorite games?

It is is a Psuedo-Sandbox game that is built on top of an interesting universe with tons of customizations and an active modding community!

The game feels liberating when you're not restricted to the main story. You are given the choice to do a side quests in your own way, discover new locations by exploring on your own, customize your weapons and built your settlement with some degree of freedom. Interactable Items and scraps scattered around the wasteland have a purpose and when you pick up that rusty can, your monkey brain just feels pure satisfaction. Also the gore system feels satisfying like blowing a raider's brains out with a shotgun using VATS.

If you just play the game as how it is, overlook many of it's flaws and don't take the story seriously, it's damn enjoyable. Now add on top of that with mods and it's guranteed you'll be having the time of your life! Bethesda should thank the Modding community for carrying this franchise!

Here's your full ghoulish rundown for Fallout 4:

Fallout 4 — RECOMMENDED

War never changes, and neither does the pull of the Commonwealth wasteland. Years after launch — and now with a free next-gen update bolted on — Fallout 4 remains one of the most dangerously addictive time-sinks Bethesda ever buried. It's flawed in ways the faithful will argue about forever, but that "just one more location" hook still sinks its claws in deeper than almost anything else on Steam.

The world is the star, and it's a masterpiece of decay. Post-apocalyptic Boston is dense, hand-crafted, and endlessly rewarding to pick apart — every collapsed subway, irradiated diner, and raider-infested skyscraper hides a little story told through environment alone. The gunplay got a massive upgrade over previous Fallouts; shooting actually feels good now, and blasting a super mutant's limbs off in slow-mo V.A.T.S. never gets old. Layer on the deep perk system, the mountains of loot, and the shockingly deep settlement-building — where you can raise entire towns from the ashes — and you've got a gameplay loop that eats weekends whole. The free next-gen update sweetened it with 60fps support and extra content, so there's never been a smoother time to go irradiate yourself.

Here's where the ghoulish honesty comes in: the RPG half took a beating, and deservedly so. Bethesda gutted the dialogue system down to a four-option wheel that often boils down to "yes," "sarcastic yes," and "yes later." The writing and main story are the weakest in the modern series, and the forced voiced protagonist boxes in the role-playing that older Fallouts did better. If you came for deep choice-and-consequence storytelling, this is the entry that traded RPG soul for shooter polish — and the trade will grate on you.

Here's your full ghoulish rundown for Fallout 4:

Fallout 4 — RECOMMENDED

War never changes, and neither does the pull of the Commonwealth wasteland. Years after launch — and now with a free next-gen update bolted on — Fallout 4 remains one of the most dangerously addictive time-sinks Bethesda ever buried. It's flawed in ways the faithful will argue about forever, but that "just one more location" hook still sinks its claws in deeper than almost anything else on Steam.

The world is the star, and it's a masterpiece of decay. Post-apocalyptic Boston is dense, hand-crafted, and endlessly rewarding to pick apart — every collapsed subway, irradiated diner, and raider-infested skyscraper hides a little story told through environment alone. The gunplay got a massive upgrade over previous Fallouts; shooting actually feels good now, and blasting a super mutant's limbs off in slow-mo V.A.T.S. never gets old. Layer on the deep perk system, the mountains of loot, and the shockingly deep settlement-building — where you can raise entire towns from the ashes — and you've got a gameplay loop that eats weekends whole. The free next-gen update sweetened it with 60fps support and extra content, so there's never been a smoother time to go irradiate yourself.

Here's where the ghoulish honesty comes in: the RPG half took a beating, and deservedly so. Bethesda gutted the dialogue system down to a four-option wheel that often boils down to "yes," "sarcastic yes," and "yes later." The writing and main story are the weakest in the modern series, and the forced voiced protagonist boxes in the role-playing that older Fallouts did better. If you came for deep choice-and-consequence storytelling, this is the entry that traded RPG soul for shooter polish — and the trade will grate on you.

[h1]War Never Changes[/h1]

As you leave Vault 111, Fallout 4 has already done something memorable. The vault doors open, you step out into the Commonwealth, and that piano begins to play.

That's one of my favorite moments in gaming.

The Commonwealth is a fantastic world to explore. Whether you're wandering through the ruins of Boston, stumbling across forgotten vaults, clearing out raider camps, or simply picking a direction and seeing what you find, Fallout 4 constantly rewards curiosity.

There's always another location over the next hill.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Exploration is King[/h2]

Bethesda has always excelled at environmental storytelling, and Fallout 4 continues that tradition.

Many of my favorite moments weren't tied to the main quest at all. They came from discovering abandoned buildings, piecing together what happened before the bombs fell, and finding unique weapons or hidden locations tucked away where most players would never think to look.

The Commonwealth feels lived in, even after the end of the world.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Built for Consoles[/h2]

My biggest criticism isn't the setting or the gameplay—it's that Fallout 4 often feels designed around console limitations.

The settlement system is fun, but build limits, object limits, and other restrictions make it feel like it never reaches its full potential. You can tell there was an ambitious idea behind it, but it always feels like you're bumping into invisible walls.

On PC, it's hard not to wonder what it could have been without those limitations.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Final Thoughts[/h2]

Is Fallout 4 the best Fallout game?

Ask ten fans and you'll probably get ten different answers.

What I can say is that it's a game I've happily spent hundreds of hours exploring, building settlements, collecting gear, and getting lost in its world.

It may not be everyone's favorite Fallout, but it's absolutely one I'd recommend to anyone looking for an open-world RPG that's easy to get immersed in.
